To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
multinational corporations are increasingly organized in a network form, where the headquarters are the hub of the network.
the multinational corporation is not an organizational form in itself, but a way of organizing and controlling the operations of a firm.
multinational corporations can be divided into three categories, namely, M-form, N-form and hybrid corporations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how multinational corporations are structured in order to cope with problems of control, coordination and integration of the international operations.
the following questions: How do we organize multinational corporations?

three main issues: 1) the development of the multinational corporation from a hierarchical to a network organization, 2) the development of new strategies, structures and control systems for managing international operations and 3) the role of information technology in managing international operations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multinational corporation has evolved from the M-form to the N-form.
the multinational corporations have developed from an M-structure, through a hybrid form, to an N-form.
the recent development in multinational corporations has been from M-form to Nform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
multinational corporations are increasingly organized as networks of autonomous business units, and that the role of headquarters is to coordinate and control these units.

the process school is a useful tool for understanding the strategies of multinational corporations, and the N-form organization is a useful tool in understanding the structures of multinational corporations.
the process school has contributed to the knowledge of how multinational corporations are formed, and how they grow.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the multinational corporation has evolved from a hierarchical, M-form structure, where the parent company controlled and coordinated its subsidiaries through a central office, to a networked, N-form structure, where subsidiaries and other units in the network have a more autonomous role in their decision-making.
there has been a shift from a hierarchical, M-Form, structure to a more decentralized, network-based, N-form structure.
the multinational corporation is still a relatively unexplored concept.
